question: The velocity of a particle is $v(t)=t^3-6t^2+9t$ m/s.(a) Find the positive instants at which its acceleration is zero.(b) Determine the velocity at each of these instants.
explanation: Acceleration functionAcceleration is the rate of change of velocity:$$a(t)=\frac{dv}{dt}=3t^2-12t+9$$Zero-acceleration condition$$3t^2-12t+9=0$$Dividing by $3$ and factorising,$$t^2-4t+3=0$$$$(t-1)(t-3)=0$$Therefore, $t=1$ second or $t=3$ seconds.Velocity at $t=1$$$v(1)=1-6+9=4\text{ m/s}$$Velocity at $t=3$$$v(3)=27-54+27=0\text{ m/s}$$Final resultThe acceleration is zero at $t=1$ and $t=3$ seconds. The corresponding velocities are $4$ m/s and $0$ m/s, respectively.

options.A:
(a) $t=1,3$ s
(b) Velocities $4$ m/s and $0$ m/s, respectively
options.B:
(a) $t=1,2$ s
(b) Velocities $4$ m/s and $-2$ m/s, respectively
options.C:
(a) $t=2,3$ s
(b) Velocities $-2$ m/s and $0$ m/s, respectively
options.D:
(a) $t=1,3$ s
(b) Velocities $0$ m/s and $4$ m/s, respectively
